reason: E2 confirms that a 2100°C/2 h homogenization was used to achieve a fully homogeneous state in specific Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-W alloys, but neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence that this treatment refines grain structure, inhibits grain-boundary sliding, or directly improves high-temperature strength relative to an as-cast baseline. E1 only reports properties of as-cast alloys without homogenization. The key mechanistic and performance premises are therefore unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Homogenization at 2100°C for 2 h yields a fully homogeneous state in refractory HEAs
Reduced microsegregation alleviates local stress concentrations and dislocation sources
Refined grain structure inhibits grain-boundary sliding at high temperature
These microstructural changes improve high-temperature strength and reduce thermal softening
